# Data Quality & Accuracy Maintenance Procedure

__ Document ID: DOC050__

__Owner__: DPO

__Version__: 1

__Reviewed by__: PIMS Manager

__Reviewed on__: 17 Nov 2025

__Approved by__: PIMS Owner

__Approved on:__ 20 Nov 2025

__Next Review Date:__ 20 Nov 2026

__1\. Purpose__

To ensure all personal data processed by Arion Networks is accurate, up to date, and relevant, in line with:

- GDPR Article 5\(1\)\(d\)
- ISO/IEC 27701:2019 A\.7\.4\.3

__2\. Scope__

Applies to:

- Data collected directly from individuals
- Client\-provided data handled under processing contracts
- Training participants and platform account data

__3\. Principles__

- Data must be:
	- Accurate and complete
	- Kept up to date where necessary
	- Corrected or deleted if inaccurate

__4\. Implementation Measures__

__4\.1 At Collection__

- Use structured forms with validation \(e\.g\., date formats, email check\)
- Collect only verifiable data where possible

__4\.2 Post\-Collection Controls__

- Allow users to view and update their data \(e\.g\., via account portal\)
- Provide clear contact for update requests \(e\.g\., privacy@arionnetworks\.com\)
- Include review cycles in data retention and DPIA evaluations

__4\.3 For Processor Data__

- Clarify in contracts who is responsible for data accuracy
- Follow client instructions for updates and corrections
- Avoid altering source data unless contractually permitted

__4\.4 Quarterly Verification \(PII Systems\)__

- During quarterly access reviews per Access Management Process, the Office Manager spot\-checks data accuracy for minimum 2 random personnel records 
- Contact details \(email, phone, address\) are verified as current 
- Any identified inaccuracies are corrected immediately 
- Results documented in Access Register \- PII Systems

__5\. Review and Correction Process__

- Any identified errors must be:
	- Logged and assessed within 2 business days
	- Corrected within 5 business days
- Correction efforts are tracked as part of the DSR R

# Data Protection Impact Assessment \(DPIA\) Procedure

__ Document ID: DOC049__

__Owner__: DPO

__Version__: 1

__Reviewed by__: PIMS Manager

__Reviewed on__: 17 Nov 2025

__Approved by__: PIMS Owner

__Approved on:__ 20 Nov 2025

__Next Review Date:__ 20 Nov 2026

## __1\. Purpose__

This procedure defines how Arion Networks conducts Data Protection Impact Assessments \(DPIAs\) to identify and mitigate privacy risks in accordance with:

- GDPR Article 35
- ISO/IEC 27701:2019 control A\.7\.2\.5
- Privacy and Information Security and Data Management Policy \(DOC003\)

## __2\. Scope__

Applies to all processing activities that may present high risk to data subject rights and freedoms, including new systems, significant changes to existing processing, or regulatory requirements\.

## __3\. When DPIA is Required__

### __3\.1 Mandatory DPIA Triggers__

DPIA must be conducted when processing:

- __High Risk to Rights and Freedoms__: New processing presents significant privacy risks
- __Significant Changes__: Major modifications to existing processing activities or technologies
- __Regulatory Requirements__: Mandated by data protection authorities or industry regulations
- __New Technology__: Implementation of new technologies that process personal data
- __Large Scale Processing__: Systematic processing of large amounts of personal data

### __3\.2 DPIA Decision Tree__

1. Does processing involve personal data? → If NO, no DPIA needed
2. Is it a new processing activity or significant change? → If NO, no DPIA needed
3. Does it present high risk to data subject rights? → If NO, document decision
4. If YES to ALL above → __DPIA Required__

## __4\. DPIA Process__

### __Step 1: Initiate DPIA__

- __Trigger__: Identified by project owner, Data Protection & Risk Manager, or during risk assessment
- __Assignment__: Data Protection & Risk Manager assigns DPIA reference ID
- __Documentation__: Log in DPIA Log Sheet

### __Step 2: Gather Information__

Complete DPIA assessmen

__Document ID: DOC057__

__Owner__: DPO

__Reviewed on__: 17 Nov 2025

__Approved by__: PIMS Owner

__Approved on:__ 20 Nov 2025

__Next Review Date:__ 20 Nov 2026

__1\. Purpose__

This procedure defines how Arion Networks s\.r\.o\. maintains its Records of Processing Activities \(RoPA\) in accordance with GDPR Article 30 and ISO/IEC 27701:2019 \(Controls A\.8\.2\.1 and A\.8\.2\.2\)\. It ensures that all personal data processing is documented, reviewed, and auditable\.

__2\. Scope__

This procedure applies to all business units, systems, processes, and services that involve the collection, use, storage, or transmission of personally identifiable information \(PII\) by Arion Networks s\.r\.o\. in the role of either PII Controller or Processor\.

__3\. Roles and Responsibilities__

Roles are stated in DOC003: [https://labguides\.sharepoint\.com/:w:/r/sites/labguide/\_layouts/15/Doc\.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B376BAAE8\-4D45\-4EF9\-BDC0\-5C4906ED7FFF%7D&file=Information%20Security%20%26%20Data%20Management%20Policy\.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true](https://labguides.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/labguide/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B376BAAE8-4D45-4EF9-BDC0-5C4906ED7FFF%7D&file=Information%20Security%20%26%20Data%20Management%20Policy.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true)

# 1\. Purpose

 This procedure defines Arion Networks' operational responsibilities when acting as a data processor, including:

- Logging processing activities \(A\.8\.3\.1\)
- Secure return or deletion of personal data upon contract termination \(A\.8\.3\.2\)
- Assisting customers with their GDPR obligations \(B\.8\.2\.1\)

Complies with ISO/IEC 27701:2019 and GDPR Article 28\(3\)\.

# 2\. Scope

Applies to all services where Arion Networks acts as a processor or subprocessor of personal data on behalf of a client \(controller\)\. Includes consulting services, SaaS tools, custom deployments,  subprocessed workstreams and eny other services involving client PII processing\.

# 3\. Logging Processing Operations \(A\.8\.3\.1\)

- Maintain a log for each client engagement where Arion processes PII
- Each log entry must include:
	- Processing purpose
	- Data categories
	- Processing duration
	- Subprocessors used
	- Security measures applied
	- Access control details
- Logs must be:
	- Created during onboarding
	- Reviewed at least annually or upon significant change
	- Retained for 5 years after end of engagement

__Fields in Processor Operations Log__

__Field__

__Description__

Client ID

Unique client identifier

Customer Name

Name of customer organization

Processing Purpose

Purposes documented in customer DPA

Service Type

e\.g\., compliance automation, vulnerability analysis

PII Categories

Data types involved

Access Control

Who had access, what level

Processing Duration

Contractual or technical lifespan

Subprocessors

Any used in processing chain

Security Controls

Summary of encryption, segregation, MFA, etc\.

## 3\.1 Purpose Limitation \(B\.8\.2\.2\)"

- Arion processes customer PII ONLY for purposes specified
